items.title: 28.5 Comparison of Three Types of Chromatography

source_refs.note: Topic 28.5 with the comparison table (PDF 183). The paragraph on choosing phases follows the learning outcome. The exercises (PDF 183-185) are not part of the lesson body.

blocks.caption: Comparison of the three types of chromatography (book's table)

blocks.text: Choosing suitable stationary and mobile phases is essential: a separation works only if the components differ in how strongly they are held by the stationary phase compared with the mobile phase. Polar substances, for example, are held strongly by a polar stationary phase such as alumina, so a less polar solvent lets them be separated from non-polar substances.

blocks.prompt: Which type of chromatography would you use to measure the proportion of each volatile ester in a mixture, and why?
blocks.explanation: Gas chromatography: it separates volatile compounds quickly and is quantitative, since peak areas give the proportion of each component.

items: Paper: partition, water in paper, slow. TLC: adsorption, silica/alumina, faster. GC: gas-liquid partition, very fast and quantitative.
